message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it might be a STEMI, right?
reply:
**I wouldn’t call this a definite STEMI from the image alone, but I can’t safely exclude an acute heart attack.**

My reading is:

- Sinus rhythm, roughly 75–80 beats/minute.
- Very high QRS voltage, with deep S waves in V1–V3 and tall R waves in V4–V6, suggesting **left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH)**.
- Some anterior ST elevation, most apparent in V2–V3. In this setting, it could represent repolarization changes associated with LVH. LVH is a recognized STEMI mimic. ([ACC/AHA guideline](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2024.11.009))

**Symptoms, comparison with an older ECG, repeat ECGs, and troponin testing are needed** to distinguish these possibilities. If there is current chest discomfort, breathlessness, sweating, or faintness, call emergency services now and don’t drive yourself. ([AHA](https://cpr.heart.org/en/-/media/Files/Health-Topics/Heart-Attack/Heart-Attack-warning-signs-infographic.pdf))

Is this ECG from someone having symptoms now, and what prompted it?
